C-FLUSH-AND-PAY.IntentSummary:
Author the execution for the approved, frozen spec `.ngrace/changes/active/C-FLUSH-AND-PAY/spec.xml` and only within it; the plan conforms to the spec, it does not extend, narrow or reinterpret it. Three sequential tasks: T-001 flushes the sixteen staged entries `f205` through `f220` into `findings.xml` and `decisions.xml` with both roots read back from the written files; T-002 mints the one chartered `C-INDEX-METRIC-2` row, rewrites the registry root by read-back, runs exactly one `bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts --retire` against the production record in the same task, and in the same task reconciles the one shipped suite pin the mint invalidates; T-003 adds the four production assertions the spec's evidence-hygiene Constraint charters to `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts`. ObservedWriteScope is exactly the seven RM-GOVERNED-PATH record files plus that one suite file — the record is in execution's write scope here (the flush, the mint and the move are task work; the authority holds no mid-execution write — its acts are approval, commit and the close). `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md` is nobody's to write: no task touches it, and pruning the flushed entries is post-merge hygiene owned by the authority. DurableScope is `<None />`: no graph module is written, no `src/` file is edited, and exactly one `scripts/` file changes — do not mint a synthetic module (the spec's AffectedAreas names none; the module-ownable predicate `isModuleOwnableWritePath`, `src/lint/core.ts:724`, never fires for these paths, so `change.graph-anchors-miss-write-scope` cannot fire for the empty anchor set).
The transient invalid state, declared (spec P1). The flush alone leaves a record the plain validator accepts: no registry row pays any flushed token before the mint — the shipped `derivePayerMap` mints 73 tokens at the base commit and the intersection with `F205` through `F220` is empty (measured by calling the shipped function over both registry layers; re-read at execution) — so the eligibility pair opens at the mint, not at the flush. Between the mint and the move the validator exits 1 with exactly two codes — `finding-eligible-still-live` for f205 (archive event C-INDEX-METRIC-2) and `registry-eligible-still-live` for the row (archive event C-INDEX-METRIC-2), the D28.1 enforcement saying the move is due — and no ceiling code: the mid-state roots fit inside every persisted window (findings base read back 7715 against the held 7846 at this plan's commit; index 272 against 296; registry 13 against 26). No task boundary and no commit sits inside that window: T-002 carries the mint, the registry root rewrite and the one `--retire` together, and the window is opened and closed inside it, as a declared, verified working-tree state, never a commit `validate:ci` can see. The decomposition cannot avoid the window — the mint necessarily creates an archive-named live row and a paid live finding, and `--retire` is the sanctioned writer of the retired sibling and of the PaidBy stamp — but it avoids opening it across any boundary, which is the strongest form available and the one the spec's ordering Constraint prescribes.
One commit, and the suite green at every boundary it leaves open (spec P2). Measured end to end on a throwaway copy of the record with the shipped CLI and shipped functions at this plan's base commit (65c99ecefe689e5da5e4370bbf79faeee991502f): the suite (`bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts`, 63 tests at the base commit) is green at HEAD, at the post-flush boundary, and at the post-move boundary once T-002's reconciliation has landed; the validator exits 0 at every boundary and only mid-window reports the two eligibility codes; preservation and citation validators exit 0 on the flushed and on the moved record; a `--retire` probe on a throwaway copy reports moved 0 both post-flush and post-move. There is therefore no boundary in this plan where the record or the suite is red; the only non-green state is inside T-002, between the mint and the move, and it is never a task boundary, never a verification point, and never a commit. The one suite test the mint invalidates — the closed-world loop of the C-RECORD-PARSE payer-derivation test — is reconciled inside T-002, in the same task, because the mint is the act that invalidates it: landing the mint without the reconciliation would leave exactly one suite failure at the T-002 boundary, and the C-INDEX-METRIC-2 precedent (its T-003 carrying the teaching-test extension and the clause it requires in one task so the boundary stays green) is the house pattern for exactly this shape.
The new assertions are read-only over the record (spec P3). T-003 appends four production assertions to `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` in the C-PAYMENT-RECORD-4 house shape: a flush invariant (each flushed id exactly once across both findings files with the agreeing index layer — the walk is the duplicate check — plus the root read-back arithmetic), a payment invariant (the row retired in `registry-retired.xml`, its derived payment set exactly `F205` by the shipped `derivePayerMap` over an isolated archive root containing exactly that name, the production map naming `F205` with this payer, f205 not live, PaidBy stamped), a production run of the shipped `validateRecordRetirement` asserting zero findings with the same call discriminating on a mutated copy, and a clamp invariant (the persisted findings headroom equals ceiling minus base and is below seven times the median live element line count, mirrored over the shipped parser because `findingLineCounts` is not exported — mirror it, do not export it, as the C-PAYMENT-RECORD-4 precedent ruled for `liveRowCount`). Each names the mutation that turns it red and both directions are driven on mutated copies during execution — never against the production record.
The clamp, not the product (spec P4). No assertion or criterion pins the formula product as the persisted headroom. The persisted findings headroom is observed as the clamp's result: it equals ceiling minus base, and it is strictly below the formula product `7 × median` over the delivered live set — the exact defect repaired in the spec before approval, not reintroduced here. At this plan's commit the throwaway drive reads post-move roots `findings 7673 / 173 / 7846`, `index 271 / 25 / 296`, `registry 12 / 14 / 26` byte-identical to the pre-bundle root, `rulings 1697 / 186 / 1883` with `rulings.xml` and `rulings-retired.xml` byte-identical throughout, the clamp binding at `7715 + 7 × 34 = 7953` against the held 7846.
Scalar occupancy figures below — the per-element line counts, the root triples, the median — are plan-time measurements marked to expire: every criterion asserts a relation its instrument can observe, the written base always comes from a read-back, and the projection is used only to check a ceiling is not breached. The buffer at this plan's commit renders every entry exactly as the spec's expiring table records — F220 at 34 lines by the shipped rule (`newlineCount` of the element span plus one), sixteen elements totalling 576, mid-state base 7715, headroom 131, post-move 7673 / 173 — re-driven twice over the buffer as it stands with the shipped parser and `computeElementSpans`, the two drives byte-identical. The earlier draft's 35-line reading of F220 is withdrawn and its cause named: a raw cut to end of file let the buffer's single terminating newline ride into the last body, which pushes `</Body>` onto its own line, adds exactly one line to F220's span alone, and reddens the byte-identity probe. The post-move median is 34 and the product 238 either way — one element does not move the median of 210 — so only the base and headroom scalars shifted, and no ratified criterion scalar depends on the withdrawn figure. The buffer is untracked and `.gitignore`d, so the figures cannot be diffed against the spec's snapshot; they are measured, not inferred, and the flush embeds the buffer as it stands.
Traps, answered from the tree. T1 (budgets): `FIX_SIGNATURE_REPEAT_BUDGET = 2` (src/grace-cursor.ts:187) and `FIX_DISTINCT_SIGNATURE_BUDGET = 4` (src/grace-cursor.ts:193) fire per task on failed verification attempts, so each task below carries one failure family — T-001 the flush write (element shape, root read-backs, byte-identity probe), T-002 the payment move (row shape, moved count, roots) plus the one-line reconciliation of the pin the mint itself invalidates, T-003 the net-new assertions. Splitting the mint from the move would put a task boundary inside the eligibility window; splitting the reconciliation from the mint would leave the T-002 boundary red by exactly one test; merging all three tasks would put three failure families in one task and spend the distinct budget on unrelated causes. T2 (what renders the flushed elements): the engine's `renderFinding` is module-private and re-escapes its input, so the task does not call it — the executor drives a throwaway inline `bun -e` script importing the shipped `parseFrozenMarkdown` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:150`) and emitting the landed house shape the predecessors calibrated: an open tag matching the landed f204 element's form, a `<Title>` carrying the heading line verbatim with the `### ` prefix riding, one `<Body>…</Body>` construct carrying the staged body embedded verbatim, with `</Body>` closing inline after the body's last byte, and the close tag; plus one index line `<Entry id="…" token="…" genre="finding" layer="live" />` per id. The bodies embed verbatim because the buffer is staged pre-escaped and the render applies no transform to body bytes at all — the shipped parser's cut is the only cut, and it never leaves the buffer's terminating end-of-file newline inside a body — guaranteed by the dated execution-time probe (T-001's criterion): each landed `<Body>`'s bytes, extracted with the shipped parser, are byte-compared against the staged bodyRaw. T3 (the root rewrites): hand-written by tasks — the findings root and the index root in T-001, the registry root in T-002, each from a read-back of its shipped metric with the ceiling byte-identical; rewritten by the move — all four live roots by `persistSnapshot` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:950-961`), findings and rulings clamped against the pre-move base read, index by `INDEX_HEADROOM_ENTRIES` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:454`), registry by the live-row rule, rulings rewritten byte-identically when nothing is eligible. The roots-invariant tripwire reads every live root at every boundary, and every hand-write sets base to its shipped metric read back, so the tripwire holds at every open boundary by construction. T4 (assertion wiring): BaselineAssertions pin the shipped pre-bundle world with existence and command pins only — no byte pin on any record file, because the record is written by tasks and a baseline byte pin would be a moving target (C-PAYMENT-RECORD-3's precedent); TargetAssertions are satisfiable at the target gate, which runs after all writes, and pin existence plus the four command evidences; the production byte-observations live in the suite T-003 adds, which is delivered last because every one of them depends on the move — nothing that depends on a later task sits in an earlier task's target assertions. T5 (the execution/close boundary): tasks emit opened (epoch open at T-001's start), progress (task start and completion), attempt (every verification cycle, with signature kind and key on fail), verification-unavailable (when evidence cannot be collected), pause and resume around interruptions, and command-run is produced by the CLI's `--run-commands` path, never hand-invented; tasks must not emit or perform anything belonging to the close — no terminal (the operator's judgment per the ngrace-execute skill's terminal entry), no cursor fold, no escalation, circuit or discarded (reserved kinds), no gate approve/verdict/apply/archive, no `ngrace supersede`, no status write, no archive move, and none of the close's own acts. T-001.Title: Flush the sixteen staged entries f205 through f220 into findings.xml and decisions.xml with both roots read back from the written files

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Flush mechanics, by anchor id and never by position. The flush set is closed by anchor id: an entry is flushed if and only if its anchor id is one of f205 through f220, matched as `` forms, and nothing else in the buffer is flushed — including entries staged after this plan was written. Render each entry by driving the shipped `parseFrozenMarkdown` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:150`) over `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md` as staged — it parses the buffer with no normalization at this plan's commit (driven; per-entry facts below expire, re-measure at execution) — and emit one landed element per entry in the house form the landed f204 element shows: open tag matching the landed predecessors' local form, `` carrying the heading line verbatim (the `### ` prefix rides along), `<Body>` on its own line and `</Body>` closing one construct around the staged body embedded verbatim — `</Body>` closes inline after the body's last byte, on the last prose line whenever the body's last line is prose — and the close tag. Cut each body where the shipped parser cuts it: at the line before the next entry's anchor, and for the last entry at end of file with the buffer's single terminating newline popped — and embed `parseFrozenMarkdown`'s `bodyRaw` verbatim. No render-time normalization exists, no transform of a body byte exists, and any non-identity transform of a body byte is a deviation. The inter-entry blank lines the shipped cut leaves inside the non-last bodies are the buffer's own bytes and ride along, exactly as the shipped `renderFinding` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:470-478`) embeds them — the spec's expiring table and its driven line arithmetic count them. The rendering is driven, not hand-typed: a throwaway inline `bun -e` script imports `parseFrozenMarkdown` and `newlineCount` from `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts` and emits the elements, so ids, slugs and tokens come from the shipped parser. If `parseFrozenMarkdown` throws (`split: missing anchor for heading at line N`, `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:182-185`), or any staged fragment citation would not resolve against the index, stop and report — never normalize away. Do not write `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md`; do not prune it; no criterion depends on the buffer's total entry count beyond the flushed ids. Append the sixteen `<Finding>` elements after the last live Finding in findings.xml (f204 at this plan's commit — re-read at execution, never trust a plan-time figure) and sixteen `<Entry id="…" token="…" genre="finding" layer="live" />` lines after the last finding `Entry` in decisions.xml, keeping the close tag's leading whitespace with the close tag. Plan-time measured facts, expiring: sixteen anchors, ids f205 through f220, all findings genre; zero raw `<` and zero bare `&` across the staged bodies; zero `[[f…]]`-form references; 22 fragment citations whose destinations are f136, f204 and f205 through f220; per-element line counts by the shipped rule (newlineCount of the element span plus one) 42, 40, 30, 44, 65, 44, 27, 25, 52, 33, 28, 33, 24, 28, 27, 34 — total 576, the spec's expiring table exactly; every figure below re-reads at execution.

Roots, read back, never projected. Write findings.xml first: append the elements, then read `newlineCount` back from the written file for the root base attribute — a written base is never derived from a projection; the projection (576 lines at this plan's commit, mid-state base 7715 against 7139) is used only to check the findings ceiling is not breached. Headroom becomes ceiling minus the read-back base; the ceiling stays byte-identical (7846 at this plan's commit) and is never raised. A read-back base above the persisted ceiling stops the task and reports; it does not raise the ceiling. Then append the sixteen `Entry` lines and derive the index root the same way: base equals the live-`Entry` count read back (272 at this plan's commit), headroom equals ceiling minus base (24), ceiling byte-identical (296). After both writes: no duplicate id in either file — the shipped parser's walk over both trees is the duplicate check. Byte-identity probe, dated to this task's window and recorded in the executor's report, never a standing criterion: for each flushed id, extract the landed `<Body>` span with the shipped parser and compare its bytes to the staged body (`parseFrozenMarkdown`'s bodyRaw, verbatim); all sixteen must be byte-identical. The mutation that reddens the probe is any altered body byte. The probe's both sides live inside this bundle's own window (F215's rule): the buffer side is pruned only post-merge, by the authority, never by a task.

Post-flush state, verified before T-002 begins. The plain validator exits 0 — the flush alone opens no eligibility, because no registry row pays any flushed token yet (the shipped `derivePayerMap` mints 73 tokens at the base commit, none of them `F205` through `F220`; re-read at execution). The preservation and citation validators exit 0 on the flushed record (the fragment citations' destinations — f136, f204 and the freshly flushed ids — all resolve; measured). The record suite is green. A `--retire` probe on a throwaway copy of the flushed record reports moved 0 and writes nothing — the flush opens no eligibility, and the probe discriminates that rather than merely running. The flushed bodies embed the corrected buffer verbatim; the buffer's staging convention (staged escapes, legal raw `>` in `->` arrows) is preserved byte-for-byte.
